extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions/recipients covered by Title IX (K-12 and postsecondary), Title IX coordinators, school employees, and institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-regulation standards for how recipients must treat applicants and students with pregnancy, pregnancy-related conditions, and parental/family/marital status under Title IX, including employee notification duties and privacy limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on pre-admission inquiries into marital status
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.21(c)(2)(iii) prohibits a recipient from making a pre-admission inquiry into the marital status of an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to add additional categories (e.g., 'current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions') to this provision because other provisions already prohibit discrimination on those bases. Recipients must not implement any policy, practice, or procedure—including pre-admission inquiries—concerning the parental, family, or marital status of a student or applicant that treats that person differently based on sex. The discussion notes Common Application data considerations but affirms the general prohibition on targeted pre-admission marital-status questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed pre-admission questions must be asked of all applicants ('all applicants' phrasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-admission question that concerns status is permissible only 'if this question is asked of all applicants' (the Department uses 'all applicants' instead of 'such applicants of both sexes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating that a question is permissible only if asked of all applicants is consistent with Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination and conveys the same point as the prior 'both sexes' phrasing. 'All applicants' is considered more inclusive and grammatically correct; it prevents asking targeted questions only of one sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity in admissions: treat pregnancy/related conditions like other temporary medical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.21(c)(1) requires that, in determining admissions, a recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions in the same manner and under the same policies and practices as any other temporary medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised wording (removing 'any temporary disability resulting therefrom' and replacing 'disability or physical condition' with 'medical conditions') to clarify scope. If a recipient provides, for example, extensions or other reasonable modifications to applicants recovering from other temporary medical conditions, it must provide the same to applicants recovering from childbirth. If the recipient has no policy/practice for temporary medical conditions, Title IX does not require it to create one; however, if a pregnancy-related condition qualifies as a disability, ADA/Section 504 obligations also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for applicants are tied to existing temporary medical condition policies (no standalone Title IX right for applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to create an independent Title IX requirement that applicants receive reasonable modifications beyond what a recipient provides for other temporary medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cited the need for more analysis on cost, administrative burden, and overlap with other laws. The final rule requires parity with existing policies for temporary medical conditions; applicants whose pregnancy-related conditions qualify as disabilities may also be entitled to accommodations under ADA/Section 504. Example: if an applicant recovering from back surgery receives an extension to submit an essay, an applicant recovering from childbirth must receive the same only insofar as the recipient's policies/practices provide it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination against parenting applicants/students based on sex or sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.21(c)(2)(i) and §106.40(a) prohibit treating parenting applicants or students differently based on sex and prohibit discrimination based on sex stereotypes (e.g., stereotypes about mothers' roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to expand regulatory text to explicitly list 'current, potential, perceived, expected, or past' parental/family/caregiver status but explained that prohibitions against sex-based differential treatment and sex stereotypes (under §106.10) already cover many concerns. The protection for parental status applies throughout a student's participation in the program or activity. The Department will refer to the definition of 'parental status' in §106.2 for specifics about non-birthing parents and caregivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on current, potential, or past pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.40(b)(1) prohibits any discrimination against a student or employee based on their 'current, potential, or past' pregnancy or related conditions; 'pregnancy or related conditions' is defined broadly in §106.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition includes pregnancy, childbirth, termination of pregnancy, lactation, medical conditions related to those states, and recovery. The Department reiterates longstanding interpretations that Title IX violations include stopping or reducing financial assistance, subjecting students to additional requirements (e.g., listing pregnancy as an athletic infraction), or excluding students from programs or activities on that basis. The Department intends to provide technical assistance and may issue guidance, including for K-12 recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee duty to provide Title IX Coordinator contact when directly informed of a student's pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.40(b)(2) requires that when a student, or a person with a legal right to act on the student's behalf, directly informs an employee that the student is pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions, the employee must promptly provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and inform the student that the Coordinator can coordinate specific actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty is triggered only when directly informed (verbally or in writing) by the student or their legal representative; overheard or secondhand information does not trigger it. The employee need not notify the Coordinator directly and need only act if they reasonably believe the Coordinator has not already been notified. The Department clarified that employees are not required to approach students unprompted, ask sensitive questions, or make assumptions. Example: a student telling a teacher 'I am pregnant...' triggers the duty; overhearing the same statement does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on employee obligations, documentation, and interaction with other duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation does not require employees to document compliance with §106.40(b)(2), does not require them to ask whether the Coordinator has been notified, and narrows the trigger to direct notification by the student or authorized person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any voluntarily maintained records would be subject to disclosure restrictions in §106.44(j). The Department declined to limit the duty to instances where the student first requests a reasonable modification, because students may be unaware of such rights; instead, employees must provide Coordinator contact information upon direct notification. Where information indicates potential sex discrimination (e.g., student reports being prohibited from trying out for a play due to pregnancy), other notification obligations (e.g., §106.44(c)) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and restrictions on disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained under these regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(j) prohibits the disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with this part, with some exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discussion clarifies that recipients should protect student privacy; records maintained in responding to pregnancy-related notifications are subject to §106.44(j)'s disclosure restrictions. The Department revised related regulatory language elsewhere (e.g., §106.40(b)(2)) to account for confidentiality concerns and to avoid mandatory documentation requirements that could create disclosure risks.
